sections.title: Code Example — Contextual Compression with LangChain
sections.body:
```python name=contextual_compression_example.py
# pip install langchain langchain-openai langchain-chroma

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_chroma import Chroma
from langchain.retrievers import ContextualCompressionRetriever
from langchain.retrievers.document_compressors import LLMChainExtractor
from langchain_core.documents import Document

# ─── LONG DOCUMENTS ───
documents = [
    Document(page_content="""
    Python was invented by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. 
    It is named after the British comedy group Monty Python. Python has 
    a simple, readable syntax that makes it beginner-friendly. 
    However, Python has significant performance limitations due to the 
    Global Interpreter Lock (GIL), which prevents multiple threads from 
    executing Python bytecode simultaneously. For CPU-intensive tasks, 
    Python can be 10-100x slower than compiled languages like C++ or Rust. 
    Despite this, Python is extremely popular in data science, machine 
    learning, and web development due to its rich ecosystem of libraries.
    """),
    Document(page_content="""
    JavaScript was created by Brendan Eich in 1995 in just 10 days.
    Originally designed only for browsers, JavaScript is now used on 
    servers via Node.js. JavaScript is single-threaded but uses an 
    event loop for asynchronous operations. This non-blocking I/O makes 
    it excellent for real-time applications. JavaScript's performance has 
    improved dramatically with V8 engine JIT compilation. TypeScript, a 
    superset of JavaScript, adds static typing for better code quality.
    React, Vue, and Angular are the most popular JavaScript frameworks.
    """),
    Document(page_content="""
    Machine learning is a branch of artificial intelligence that enables 
    systems to learn from data. Supervised learning uses labeled training 
    data. Unsupervised learning finds patterns without labels. 
    Reinforcement learning trains through rewards. Deep learning, a 
    subset of ML, uses neural networks with many layers. The transformer 
    architecture revolutionized NLP with models like BERT and GPT. 
    Training large models requires massive GPU compute power and energy.
    Overfitting occurs when models memorize training data and fail to 
    generalize to new examples.
    """),
]

# ─── SETUP ───
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
vectorstore = Chroma.from_documents(documents, embeddings)
base_retriever = vectorstore.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 2})

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini", temperature=0)

# ─── COMPRESSOR ───
compressor = LLMChainExtractor.from_llm(llm)

# ─── COMPRESSION RETRIEVER ───
compression_retriever = ContextualCompressionRetriever(
    base_compressor=compressor,
    base_retriever=base_retriever
)

def compare_standard_vs_compressed(query: str):
    print(f"\n{'='*65}")
    print(f"🔍 Query: '{query}'")
    print('='*65)
    
    print("\n📄 Standard Retrieval (Full Documents):")
    std_results = base_retriever.invoke(query)
    for i, doc in enumerate(std_results, 1):
        print(f"\n  [{i}] ({len(doc.page_content)} chars):")
        print(f"  {doc.page_content.strip()[:200]}...")
    
    print("\n\n🗜️  Contextual Compression (Relevant Parts Only):")
    comp_results = compression_retriever.invoke(query)
    for i, doc in enumerate(comp_results, 1):
        print(f"\n  [{i}] ({len(doc.page_content)} chars):")
        print(f"  {doc.page_content.strip()}")

compare_standard_vs_compressed("What are the performance issues in Python?")
compare_standard_vs_compressed("How does JavaScript handle async operations?")
```
